_label: OFFLINE FIXTURE - hand-written expected assessment for examples/orders-service. NOT model output; replayed through the fake session protocol to exercise the pipeline.
name: checkpoint-idempotency-fixed

submission.summary: createOrder now sends the same Idempotency-Key on every attempt, and the duplicate-order experiment produces one order. The earlier findings are resolved. One open question: the key is generated per placeOrder call, not per checkout.

findings.title: Idempotency key is per placeOrder call, not per checkout
findings.statement: placeOrder generates a new randomUUID() on each call. Retries inside one call are deduplicated, but if the storefront calls placeOrder again for the same checkout (double submit, page retry after an error), a new key creates a new order.
findings.failure_case: The checkout page calls placeOrder again after a failure the user sees (for example a page retry); a new key is generated, so the second call creates a second order.
findings.controls_checked: The key is reused across retries inside one placeOrder call; nothing ties it to the checkout across calls.
findings.why_it_matters: The goal is one order per checkout, not per call. Whether this matters depends on how the storefront calls placeOrder.

evidence.quote: a unique string per checkout attempt

findings.uncertainty: Depends on storefront behaviour that is not in this repository.
findings.suggested_next_action: If the storefront can resubmit, derive the key from a stable checkout id passed in by the caller.

resolved.reason: createOrder sends one Idempotency-Key across retries; experiment shows 1 order.
A timed-out create is now retried with the same key and replayed, so the outcome is reconciled.
